reader.requirement: At --std 85, THRU and THROUGH must be interchangeable in the format-2 (condition-name) VALUE clause, after VALUE IS or VALUES ARE, for numeric (including signed) and nonnumeric ranges, one or several in a series. Each spelling must give the same condition test and SET result, and both must be refused where format 2 does not apply (a non-88 entry).

edition-consulted.switches: word status of THRU / THROUGH (both reserved at 85, the same as 2023, ReservedWords.Table.cs#Entries)

reader.edition-search: grep valueClauseRange over Compiler/Frontend C#: BindCondition and the VALUE placement screens read the range node and never the token, and no DialectLevel test guards the range
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers numeric ranges after VALUE. Nonnumeric ranges, signed literals, VALUES ARE, mixing both spellings in one clause, SET TO TRUE and the non-88 refusal are not exercised.

probes.printed: FTTTFFFFF FTTTFFFFF TTFTTFFFT / NEG-IN / NEG-OUT / NEG-END / SET=B
probes.expected: "B" THRU "D" and VALUES ARE "B" THROUGH "D" give the same image over ABCDEFGHZ; a mixed list "A" THRU "B", "D" THROUGH "E" "Z" is true at A,B,D,E,Z; -5 THRU -1 and -5 THROUGH -1 agree inside, outside and at the end value; SET to TRUE stores the first literal "B" (§1985:VI.5.15.3 SR1)

probes.printed: COBOL2167 on A1 (VALUE 1 THRU 5) and A2 (VALUE 1 THROUGH 5), level 1
probes.expected: both spellings refused outside a condition-name entry (format 1 has only literal-1)

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.5.15.3 SR1  (5.15.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1

reader.notes: valueClauseRange takes (THRU | THROUGH) as one alternative, and the binder reads only operand(0) and operand(1), so the spellings cannot diverge. The two probe images were checked by hand against the range rule.

refuter.evidence: rva3 (run, --std 85): figurative constants in ranges with both spellings (LOW-VALUE THRU "M", "N" THROUGH HIGH-VALUE, SPACE THROUGH "!", ZERO THRU 9, ZEROES THROUGH 9, 100 THRU 199) and a 77-level 88 mixing THROUGH/THRU without commas; printed 'LOhisp / loHIsp / LOhiSP / Z0 / Y0 / nZ150 / Y150 / nY-1 / +000 / S35 / nS20 / 10', all correct by hand. rva1: SPACE THRU SPACES refused COBOL2961 (correct by §1985:VI.5.15.5 GR2, literal-2 must be less). rva2: WHEN SET TO FALSE (2002 phrase) after a THRU range and after a THROUGH range both refused COBOL0900 (class c); VALUES on a format-1 entry refused COBOL2177. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.5.15.3 SR1; OK §1985:VI.5.15.5 GR2.
